ἔθνος.long: a race, people, nation; the nations, heathen world, Gentiles.
ἔθνος.sd: a race (as of the same habit), i.e. a tribe; specially, a foreign (non-Jewish) one (usually, by implication, pagan)
ἔθνος.as:
ἔθνος, -ους, τό,
[in LXX chiefly for עַם ,גּוֹי ;]
1.a multitude, a company, whether of beasts or men (Hom.).
2.a nation, people: Mt 21:4324:7, Mk 13:8, Lk 22:25, Ac 10:35, al.; in sing., of the Jewish people, Lk 7:523:2, Jo 11:48, 50-5318:35, Ac 10:2224:3, 1026:428:19.
3. In pl., as in OT, τὰ ἔ. (like Heb. הַגּוֹיִם), the nations, as distinct from Israel, Gentiles: Mt 4:156:32, Ac 26:17, Ro 3:2911:1115:10, Ga 2:8, al.; of Gentile Christians, Ro 11:1315:2716:4, Ga 2:12, 14, Eph 3:1.
SYN.: λαός (v. DCG, ii, 229; Cremer, 226).

ἐθνικός.g: pagan, heathen, gentile; a Gentile, non-Jew
ἐθνικός.long: pagan, heathen, gentile; subst: a Gentile, non-Jew.
ἐθνικός.as:
**† ἐθνικός, -ή, -όν, (< ἔθνος), [in Al.: Le 21:7 * ;]
1.national (Polyb.).
2.foreign (gramm.); in NT, as subst., ὁ ἐ., the Gentile (the adj. "describes character rather than mere position"; cf. ἔθνος, and v. Cremer, 228): Mt 5:476:718:17, III Jo 7.†

ἔθος.long: a custom, habit; an institute, rite.
ἔθος.sd: a usage (prescribed by habit or law)
ἔθος.as:
** ἔθος, -εος (-ους), τό
(< ἔθω), [in LXX: Wi 14:16, Da TH Bel 15, I Mac 10:89, II Mac 11:2513:4, IV Mac 18:5א R* ;]
habit, custom; Lk 22:39, Jo 19:40, Ac 16:2125:16, He 10:25; in Lk 1:92:42, Ac 6:1415:121:2126:328:17, almost in the narrower sense of law (Deiss., BS, 251 f.).†

ἐθίζω.sd: to accustom, i.e. (neuter passive participle) customary
ἐθίζω.as:
** ἐθίζω,
(< ἔθος), [in LXX: Si 23:9, 13, II Mac 14:30 ;]
to accustom: pass. pf. ptcp., τὸ εἰθισμένον, the established custom, Lk 2:27.†

ἐθνάρχης.long: an ethnarch, tribal lord, a subordinate ruler.
ἐθνάρχης.sd: the governor (not king) of a district
ἐθνάρχης.as:
**† ἐθνάρχης, -ου, ὁ
(< ἔθνος, ἄρχω), [in LXX: I Mac 14:4715:1, 2 * ;]
an ethnarch, a provincial governor (cf. I Mac, ll. c.; FlJ, Ant., xiii, 6, 6; Dalman, 332): II Co 11:32.†

ἐθνικῶς.long: in the manner of Gentiles, like the rest of the world.

ἐθελοθρησκία.sd: voluntary (arbitrary and unwarranted) piety, i.e. sanctimony
ἐθελοθρησκία.as:
*† ἐθελο-θρησκία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ,
self-imposed worship: Col 2:23 (eccl.; cf. DB, iv, 923a; Cremer, 733).†
